title: “Uptown Funk” by Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars
text: "Uptown Funk" is a song by British-American DJ and record producer Mark Ronson featuring American singer Bruno Mars. It was released on 10 November 2014, as the lead single from Ronson's fourth studio album, Uptown Special.
listen: Uptown Funk Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars

title: “Thinking Out Loud” by Ed Sheeran
text: "Thinking Out Loud" is a song by English singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran recorded for his second studio album, ×. It was written by Sheeran and Amy Wadge, and produced by frequent collaborator Jake Gosling.

title: “See You Again” by Wiz Khalifa featuring Charlie Puth
text: "See You Again" is a song by American rapper Wiz Khalifa featuring American singer-songwriter Charlie Puth. Produced by Puth, DJ Frank E and Andrew Cedar, who also co-wrote the song with Khalifa, the song was commissioned for the soundtrack of the 2015 film Furious 7 as a tribute to Fast & Furious actor Paul Walker, who died in a single-vehicle crash on November 30, 2013.
listen: See You Again Wiz Khalifa featuring Charlie Puth

title: “Trap Queen” by Fetty Wap
text: "Trap Queen" is the debut single by American rapper Fetty Wap from his self-titled debut album. Following its online premiere in March 2014, it was released independently on April 22, 2014, before being re-released in conjunction with 300 Entertainment on December 15, 2014.

title: “Sugar” by Maroon 5
text: "Sugar" is a song by the American rock band Maroon 5 from their fifth studio album V. It was written by Mike Posner, Adam Levine, Dr.

title: “Shut Up and Dance” by Walk the Moon
text: "Shut Up and Dance" is a song by American pop rock band Walk the Moon from their third studio album Talking Is Hard (2014). It was written by the band members and songwriters Ben Berger and Ryan McMahon.
wiki: Shut Up and Dance (Walk the Moon song)
listen: Shut Up and Dance Walk the Moon

title: “Blank Space” by Taylor Swift
text: "Blank Space" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and the second single from her fifth studio album, 1989. She wrote the song with its producers, Max Martin and Shellback.

title: “Watch Me” by Silentó
text: "Watch Me"") is the debut single by American rapper Silentó. In March 2015, he was signed to Capitol Records, which released the track as a single with an accompanying music video.

title: “Earned It” by The Weeknd
text: "Earned It", alternatively titled "Earned It", is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd. The song was released as the lead single from the soundtrack to the 2015 film Fifty Shades of Grey and was included on the Weeknd's second studio album Beauty Behind the Madness (2015).

title: “The Hills”
text: "The Hills" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd. It was released on May 27, 2015, as the second single from his second studio album, Beauty Behind the Madness.

title: “Cheerleader (Felix Jaehn Remix)” by OMI
text: "Cheerleader" is a song recorded by Jamaican singer Omi. The track was written and produced by OMI and Clifton Dillon, Mark Bradford, and Ryan Dillon.

title: “Can't Feel My Face” by The Weeknd
text: "Can't Feel My Face" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd from his second studio album, Beauty Behind the Madness. The song was released on June 8, 2015, as the album's third single.
listen: Can't Feel My Face The Weeknd

title: “Love Me Like You Do” by Ellie Goulding
text: "Love Me like You Do" is a song recorded by the English singer-songwriter Ellie Goulding for the soundtrack to the film Fifty Shades of Grey. The song was written by Savan Kotecha, Ilya Salmanzadeh, Tove Lo, Max Martin and Ali Payami; the latter two also produced it.
listen: Love Me Like You Do Ellie Goulding

title: “Take Me to Church” by Hozier
text: "Take Me to Church" is a song by Irish singer-songwriter Hozier. It was released as his debut single on 13 September 2013, originally featuring on his extended play of the same name, before being featured as the opening track of his 2014 self-titled debut album.

title: “Bad Blood” by Taylor Swift featuring Kendrick Lamar
text: "Bad Blood" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift from her fifth studio album, 1989. She wrote the song with the Swedish producers Max Martin and Shellback.
listen: Bad Blood Taylor Swift featuring Kendrick Lamar

title: “Lean On” by Major Lazer and DJ Snake featuring MØ
text: "Lean On" is a song by American electronic dance music group Major Lazer and French DJ and record producer DJ Snake featuring Danish singer MØ. It was released on March 2, 2015, as the lead single from Major Lazer's third studio album, Peace Is the Mission. It was written by MØ, Diplo, DJ Snake, Tchami, and Jr Blender, and produced by Major Lazer and DJ Snake.
listen: Lean On Major Lazer and DJ Snake featuring MØ

title: “Want to Want Me” by Jason Derulo
text: "Want to Want Me" is a song recorded by American singer Jason Derulo for his fourth studio album, Everything Is 4. It was released as the album's lead single on March 9, 2015.
listen: Want to Want Me Jason Derulo

title: “Shake It Off” by Taylor Swift
text: "Shake It Off" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and the lead single from her fifth studio album, 1989. She wrote the lyrics by herself and composed the melody with the song's producers, Max Martin and Shellback.

title: “Where Are Ü Now” by Jack Ü featuring Justin Bieber
text: "Where Are Ü Now" is a song produced by American EDM duo Jack Ü, composed of DJs and producers Skrillex and Diplo, with Canadian singer Justin Bieber. The song was released as the second single from the duo's debut studio album, Skrillex and Diplo Present Jack Ü, on their respective labels Owsla and Mad Decent, and is later included on Bieber's fourth studio album, Purpose (2015).
listen: Where Are Ü Now Jack Ü featuring Justin Bieber

title: “Fight Song” by Rachel Platten
text: "Fight Song" is a song by American singer-songwriter Rachel Platten, released on February 19, 2015, through Columbia Records. The song was included on Platten's debut extended play of the same name (2015), and her third studio album, Wildfire (2015).

title: “679” by Fetty Wap featuring Remy Boyz
text: "679" is the second single by American rapper and singer Fetty Wap from his self-titled debut album. The song features rap duo Remy Boyz, which consists of rappers Monty and P-Dice.

title: “Lips Are Movin” by Meghan Trainor
text: "Lips Are Movin" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Meghan Trainor, taken from her debut major-label studio album, Title. It was written by Trainor and the album's producer, Kevin Kadish.

title: “Worth It” by Fifth Harmony featuring Kid Ink
text: "Worth It" is a song by American girl group Fifth Harmony, featuring American rapper Kid Ink. It impacted American rhythmic crossover radio on March 2, 2015, as the third and final single from the group's debut studio album, Reflection.
listen: Worth It Fifth Harmony featuring Kid Ink

title: “Post to Be” by Omarion featuring Chris Brown and Jhené Aiko
text: "Post to Be" is a song by American singer Omarion featuring fellow American singers Chris Brown and Jhené Aiko from the former's fourth studio album, Sex Playlist. Each of the artists featured co-wrote the song alongside Ty Dolla $ign and producer DJ Mustard.
listen: Post to Be Omarion featuring Chris Brown and Jhené Aiko

title: May 19–23 – The Eurovision Song Contest 2015 is held in Vienna, Austria, and is won by Swedish entrant Måns Zelmerlöw with the song "Heroes".
text: Måns Petter Albert Sahlén Zelmerlöw is a Swedish singer and television presenter. He took part in Idol 2005, eventually finishing fifth, won the first season of Let's Dance, and scored a hit with his 2007 song "Cara Mia", which was his entry in that year's Melodifestivalen.

title: The second round of the 2015 Polish presidential election is held, with Andrzej Duda reigning victorious over then-incumbent president Bronisław Komorowski.
text: Andrzej Sebastian Duda is a Polish lawyer and politician who served as the 6th president of Poland from 2015 to 2025. Before becoming president, he served as a Member of the Sejm (MP) from 2011 to 2014 and as a Member of the European Parliament (MEP) from 2014 to 2015.

title: The FIFA President Sepp Blatter announces his intention to resign amidst an FBI-led corruption investigation, and calls for an extraordinary congress to elect a new president as soon as possible.
text: The president of FIFA serves as the chief executive of the governing body of world association football. There have been 9 presidents in FIFA's history.

title: The governments of India and Bangladesh officially ratify their 1974 agreement to exchange enclaves along their border.
text: The India–Bangladesh enclaves, also known as the Chiṭmahals and sometimes called Pasha enclaves, were the enclaves along the Bangladesh–India border, in Bangladesh and the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura, Assam and Meghalaya. title: June 12–28 – The inaugural European Games are held in Baku, Azerbaijan.
text: The 1st European Games, also known as the 2015 European Games or Baku 2015 (Azerbaijani: Bakı 2015), were the inaugural edition of the European Games, an international multi-sport event for athletes representing the National Olympic Committees (NOCs) of the European Olympic Committees. title: Pope Francis releases the encyclical letter Laudato si', dated May 24, 2015.
text: Pope Francis was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from his election in 2013 until his death in 2025. He was the first Jesuit pope, the first Latin American, and the first pope born or raised outside Europe since the 8th-century Syrian pope Gregory III. title: Kobanî massacre: ISIL fighters detonate three car bombs, enter Kobanî, Syria, and open fire at civilians, killing more than 220 people.
text: The Kobanî massacre was a combination of suicide missions and attacks on Kurdish civilians by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant on the Kurdish-majority city of Kobanî, beginning on Thursday, 25 June 2015, and culminating on Friday, 26 June 2015. The attacks continued into 28 June 2015, with the last remaining ISIL militant being killed on the following day.

title: Sousse attacks: 22-year-old Seifeddine Rezgui opens fire at a tourist resort at Port El Kantaoui, Tunisia, killing 38 people.
text: Port El Kantaoui is a tourist complex 10 kilometres north of Sousse city in central Tunisia. It was built in 1979 specifically as a tourist center, around a large artificial harbour that provides mooring with 340 berths for luxury yachts, hosting sporting activities from water skiing to paragliding, and several golf courses.

title: Kuwait mosque bombing: A suicide bomber attacks the Shia Mosque Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq at Kuwait City, Kuwait, killing 27 people and injuring 227 others.
text: The 2015 Kuwait mosque bombing was a suicide bombing took place on 26 June 2015 at a Shia mosque in Kuwait City, Kuwait. The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant claimed responsibility for the attack.

title: Cuba becomes the first country in the world to eradicate mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis.
text: A vertically transmitted infection is an infection caused by pathogenic bacteria or viruses that use mother-to-child transmission, that is, transmission directly from the mother to an embryo, fetus, or baby during pregnancy or childbirth. It can occur when the mother has a pre-existing disease or becomes infected during pregnancy.

title: An extra leap second (23:59:60) is added to end of June. The last time this occurred was in 2012.
text: Leap seconds or intercalary seconds were one-second adjustments occasionally applied to Coordinated Universal Time between 1972 and 2016, to accommodate the difference between International Atomic Time (TAI), as measured precisely by atomic clocks, and observed solar time (UT1), which varies due to irregularities and long-term slowdown in the Earth's rotation. title: Greek government-debt crisis: Greece becomes the first advanced economy to miss a payment to the International Monetary Fund in the 71-year history of the IMF.
text: Greece faced a sovereign debt crisis in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis. Widely known in the country as The Crisis, it forced the government to carry out a series of sudden reforms and austerity measures, concurrently with loss of income and property.
